subject: Immediate: Unscheduled compatibility override & rollback instructions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Anna Cruz <anna@acme.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate: Unscheduled compatibility override & rollback instructions

Hi Anna —

Quick heads-up from Redwood: we identified a compatibility regression affecting a small set of Dedicated pools running quantized variants of open-llama-13b when sequence length exceeds ~2k tokens. Symptoms we saw: truncated or repeated output, and in rare cases non-deterministic token shifts for prompts that include long system instructions.

We are deploying an unscheduled short-notice hotfix (a compatibility override that reverts a kernel-level optimization introduced in the last runtime rev). The rollout window is starting at 09:45 PT and will target a canary ring first (2 nodes in us-west-2), followed by a full push if metrics look stable. Expected interruption: brief in-flight request retries for affected nodes; we will keep the overall window to ~20 minutes.

Actions for you:
- If you can, run the attached verification prompt (hotfix_patch_notes_v1.txt) on a representative job before 09:40 and paste the result. That helps us confirm impact surface.
- If you prefer we do NOT touch your registered Dedicated nodes during the window, please reply "opt-out" by 09:30 and we will pause on your capacity (we will then schedule a targeted maintenance).

We have attached the rollback_playbook.pdf and a canary-verification-checklist for transparency. If this hotfix affects any scheduled critical jobs for Acme AI, let me know immediately and we will prioritize a rollback for your capacity and offer a service credit for any measurable degradation.

I will send live updates to this thread.

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: RE: Immediate: Unscheduled compatibility override & rollback instructions

Marissa / team —

Quick technical note for the thread and for the customer: the root trigger is a kernel selection path that under certain quantization/kv-cache alignment patterns causes misaligned KV reads after prefix compaction. The hotfix flips a compatibility flag to force the previous alignment behavior; it is non-destructive and reversible.

Runbook (high-level):
- Stage 0 (09:45): apply override to canary nodes (us-west-2, node ids: cw-218*, cw-219*).
- Monitor metric: kv_cache_mismatch_rate, prefix_mismatch_count, inference_error_5xx.
- Verification: run the checklist in canary-verification-checklist.txt — compare outputs against baseline for token-level divergence.
- Rollback: execute rollback_playbook.pdf if mismatch_rate increases post-override. Rolling back should take <10 minutes per node.

Customer communication: offer opt-out; if they opt-out we will schedule a targeted patch in the next maintenance window (ETA 48 hours) or arrange a private patch at their convenience. For any confirmed impact we will provide a 2-hour service credit and a follow-up postmortem.

Steph will lead the postmortem and customer-facing incident report. David, please standby for log bundles and CORS if Acme requests deeper forensics.

Karthik
Sr. Engineering Manager, Runtime — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Immediate: Unscheduled compatibility override & rollback instructions

Anna —

Follow-up: we ran the canary and observed the expected normalization of token alignment within 6 minutes of the override. No increase in 5xx and kv_cache_mismatch_rate dropped to baseline. Given your 10:00 workload, we did not push the override to Acme AI's Dedicated nodes (per your opt-out reply received at 09:35).

Timeline summary:
- 09:12: initial customer alert sent.
- 09:45: canary override applied (us-west-2), verification started.
- 09:55: token alignment normalized on canary; metrics stable.
- 13:00: confirmed Acme opted out; no changes made to your registered capacity.

Next steps:
- We will schedule a targeted maintenance for Acme within 48 hours. Karthik and Stephanie will own validation; we will share a tailored verification checklist and a remediation timeline.
- Stephanie will run a formal postmortem and share the interim incident report at the link below; we will include action items and proposed controls to avoid similar regressions.

Interim report: https://redwood.app/s/support/INC-9876
Postmortem meeting (invite to follow): week of Jun 3, 2029 (please indicate preferred times)

Apologies again for the short notice — we know this is disruptive and appreciate the quick coordination.

Best,
